Subject: High latency and 502s from our reserved pool — urgent

Marissa —

We started seeing a spike of 502 errors and token-level latency on our production routes backed by the reserved capacity this morning (08:00 PDT -> ongoing). Throughput is fine from our side, but 90th/95th p99 latencies are up ~2.8x and ~502 responses are correlated with long KV cache misses. Example windows: 07:58–08:06 saw a 7% 502 rate and mean response +5s. The problems are concentrated on model: gptx-4-std (pinned for our reserved pool).

Attached is a short log excerpt and a dashboard snapshot. We're now hitting user-facing retries and our ingestion pipeline is backing up. Can Redwood confirm whether this is a serving-side capacity or routing issue? This is customer-impacting.

We need an acknowledgement and ETA for mitigation.

—Daniel

Subject: INTERNAL: FastPay reserved pool — triage + immediate mitigations

Team — forwarding FastPay's alert (below). TL;DR: high p95/p99 latency and a non-trivial 502 rate on the reserved pool pinned to gptx-4-std; customer is experiencing user-impacting retries. They are a reserved customer (monthly commit FP-2027-09).

Immediate objectives:
1) Determine whether reserved workers are under-provisioned or under-scheduled for their pool. Check allocation for sequence-length-heavy requests.
2) If scheduling/under-scheduling is the root cause, temporarily increase reserved worker count for FastPay's pool and enable routing to fallback variant (gptx-4-std-q4) for non-critical routes.
3) If fallback causes quality regressions, throttle burst concurrency instead of model swap and provide per-route rate-limiting as an interim.
4) Prepare incident notes and timeframe for exec update if we confirm reserved throughput shortfall.

Important constraints: FastPay cannot accept degraded model outputs for certain routes (payment authorizations). Any fallback must be scoped to non-critical routes only. Confirm which route IDs are critical ASAP.

Attachments: forwarding customer's log excerpt.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: INTERNAL: FastPay reserved pool — triage + immediate mitigations

Quick triage update —

What we found:
- Scheduler under-allocation for FastPay's reserved pool when average seq-length > 1024. A regression in the scheduler's bin-packing heuristics (INF-4421) misclassifies high-seq requests leading to fewer reserved workers being kept warm.
- When the warm-worker ratio drops below threshold, prefix cache misses spike which increases tail latency and produces transient 502s under load.

Immediate mitigations executed (11:05–11:25):
- Bumped reserved worker count for FastPay's pool by +30% (temporary) and disabled aggressive preemption for that pool.
- Added a short-lived routing rule to divert non-payment authorization routes to gptx-4-std-q4 in the us-west region.
- Enabled request-level token-bucketing to cap concurrent requests per route to limit cascading retries.

Status now:
- 502 rate down from 7% -> 0.9% in the last 15 minutes. p95 latency improved by ~35%; p99 improving but still elevated.

Next steps:
- Priyom to prepare a patch for the scheduler heuristics (root cause) targeting deploy in next 6 hours (hotfix).
- We'll run a controlled drain test before we fully revert the temporary capacity bump.
- Marissa: recommend an executive note to FastPay summarizing actions and SLA impact. Vivek — can you own the exec-communication if we need to offer credits or other remediation?

Attached: latency_dashboard.png (last 2 hours).

—David
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

What we changed (completed):
- Temporarily increased FastPay's reserved worker headroom by +30% to recover warm-worker ratios.
- Redirected non-critical routes to an equivalent variant (gptx-4-std-q4) to reduce pressure on the pinned model.
- Implemented request-level concurrency caps to reduce cascading retries.

Immediate impact:
- 502s reduced to ~1% and p95 latency has improved ~35% over the worst window. Your ingestion backlog should clear now — please confirm.

Root cause and timeline:
- Root cause is a scheduler bin-packing regression under high sequence-length workloads (INF-4421). Engineering is preparing a hotfix; target deploy within 6 hours. We will run a controlled revert/drain afterwards and keep you in the loop.

Executive note / SLA:
